overview: The Delhi Sultanate comprised five successive Muslim dynasties that ruled northern India for over three centuries. It introduced Persian culture, Islamic architecture and new administrative systems, creating a distinctive Indo-Islamic synthesis.

items.text: Construction of the Qutb Minar begins, becoming the world's tallest brick minaret at 73 meters.
Indo-Islamic architecture develops, blending Persian, Central Asian and Indian building traditions.
Sufi mystics spread Islamic teachings through devotional poetry and music.
Hindu and Islamic artistic and intellectual traditions interact and cross-pollinate.
Persian revenue administration and land survey methods introduced to India.
New crops and irrigation techniques brought from Central Asia and Persia.
Indo-Islamic culture shaped the later Mughal civilization.
Persian language and administrative practices influenced Indian governance for centuries.

fall.text: Babur defeated the last Delhi Sultan Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat.
